title: Forbidden stars in multidimensional $0$-$1$ matrices and visibility of lattice points
summary: A $d$-dimensional $0$-$1$ matrix $M$ of size $n_1\times n_2\times \dots \times n_d$ can be considered as a Boolean function $M: B(n_1\times n_2\times \dots \times n_d) \to \{ 0,1\}$, where $B$ is the $d$-dimensional box of lattice points $(x_1, \dots, , x_d)\in Z^d$ with $0\leq x_i \leq n_i-1$, $1\leq i\leq d$. The $0$-$1$ matrix $M$ can also be described as a subset $P:=P(M)$ of $B$ such that $x\in P$ if and only if $M(x)=1$. A $k$-star with center $p$ in $M$ corresponds to a $(k+1)$-element subset $\{ p, p_1, \dots , p_k\} \subset B$ such that $p$ and $p_i$ differ only in one coordinate…
